PC-POL-024.explanation: When the insurer cancels, the insured gets the full unearned premium in proportion to the time remaining. Washington requires the pro rata refund (RCW 48.18.290(4)) and, for homeowners, dwelling fire and private auto, payment within 45 days of the cancellation notice.

PC-AUTO-016.explanation: A vehicle is uninsured when there is no liability policy, the insurer denies coverage or is insolvent, or it is a hit-and-run vehicle; equal limits make it insured. Washington's statute folds all of these into underinsured motorist coverage and counts an insolvent liability insurer's vehicle as underinsured (RCW 48.22.040).

excluded.PC-POL-025: Says an insured's cancellation is refunded short rate with a penalty. For homeowners, dwelling fire and private auto, RCW 48.18.300(2) requires a pro rata refund of at least 90 to 97 percent, so the key is wrong for those lines in Washington.
excluded.PC-AUTO-015: Says UM pays bodily injury only; Washington's required UIM also covers property damage (RCW 48.22.030(2)).
excluded.PC-AUTO-017: Distractor 'the at-fault driver has no insurance at all' is also correct in Washington, where an underinsured motor vehicle includes one with no liability insurance (RCW 48.22.030(1)).
excluded.PC-AUTO-018: Stacking item keys 'varies by state'; Washington allows anti-stacking language (RCW 48.22.030(5), (6)), so a Washington form should not answer 'varies'.
excluded.PC-AUTO-030: ISO PAP reasons for cancellation after 60 days include misrepresentation; RCW 48.18.291(2) allows only nonpayment or license suspension or revocation.
excluded.PC-LIA-015: Workers' compensation: Washington is a monopolistic state fund state (Title 51 RCW, Department of Labor and Industries) and the P&C outline has no workers' compensation section.

excluded.PC-LIA-017: Workers' compensation employers liability limits; same reason as PC-LIA-015.

excluded.PC-LIA-019: Workers' compensation exclusive remedy; same reason as PC-LIA-015.
